title: Adoption, reach and sustainability of interdisciplinary deprescribing rounds in three long-term care homes: an implementation study
abstract: Objective: to evaluate whether monthly interdisciplinary deprescribing rounds with a named deputy and a protected slot can be adopted and sustained in three long-term care homes, and how many residents they reach. Design: implementation study organised by RE-AIM using routine records, January to December 2027. Results and conclusions will be written after the year.
introduction: Residents of long-term care take many medicines that may no longer serve them. Retrieved studies show that interdisciplinary rounds can reach most residents, but that rounds stop when their pharmacist leaves, and that effects on falls are uncertain.
methods: Monthly rounds with a checklist in three homes; outcomes of reach, adoption, recommendations carried out and fidelity from round notes and administration records; falls and restarts as balancing measures. The evaluation was determined to be quality assurance (QA-2026-077).
results: No data have been collected yet. The report will present reach by home, rounds held per month, recommendations carried out, fidelity, medicine counts and balancing measures.
discussion: The discussion will focus on what sustained the rounds, who was not reached, and what the operator should decide, without attributing clinical change to the rounds.
limitations: No comparison group; documentation-based fidelity; three homes of one operator.
conclusion: To be written after the year; it will address implementation outcomes and balancing measures.
summary: StaRI-structured draft with results left empty.
